title: StableI2I: Spotting Unintended Changes in Image-to-Image Transition
claim: Conventional quality metrics rate a flawed edit above a faithful one, while our fidelity-aware evaluator ranks them correctly.
layout: 3 columns by stacked rows, top-to-bottom, metric scores then verdict bubbles with emoji reactions
description: A grid with three columns: the input image, GPT-Image-1's output and Nano-Banana's output. The photo shows a sunset beach scene with a small building. The prompt asks to replace the building with a large tree. The top row holds the three photos. GPT-Image-1's output has a dashed outline marking a removed fence and a caption saying the structure was unintentionally repainted. Blue header bars label the columns. Below them, a green prompt box sits under the input. Conventional metric scores (CLIP-IQA, MANIQA, MUSIQ, ArtiMuse, ImgEdit-Judge) appear in green for GPT-Image-1 and in gray for Nano-Banana. A blue bubble reads "GPT-Image-1 is better! / Are you kidding me?". An orange StableI2I row lists semantic, structure and low-level appearance verdicts, with errors in red. A second blue bubble reads "Nano-Banana is better! / You are an expert!". The eye goes first to the photos, then to the contrasting score panels.
caption: Qualitative image editing results from GPT-Image-1 and Nano-Banana, with scores from multiple evaluation metrics. CLIP-IQA [ref], MANIQA [ref], and MUSIQ [ref] are conventional IQA metrics, while ArtiMuse [ref] is a recent IAA metric. ImgEdit-Judge [ref] reports scores under the Physical & Detail Coherence dimension. In contrast, StableI2I more accurately assesses content fidelity and consistency.
abstract: In most real-world image-to-image (I2I) scenarios, existing evaluations primarily focus on instruction following and the perceptual quality or aesthetics of the generated images. However, they largely fail to assess whether the output image preserves the semantic correspondence and spatial structure of the input image. To address this limitation, we propose StableI2I, a unified and dynamic evaluation framework that explicitly measures content fidelity and pre--post consistency across a wide range of I2I tasks without requiring reference images, including image editing and image restoration. In addition, we construct StableI2I-Bench, a benchmark designed to systematically evaluate the accuracy of MLLMs on such fidelity and consistency assessment tasks. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that StableI2I provides accurate, fine-grained, and interpretable evaluations of content fidelity and consistency, with strong correlations to human subjective judgments. Our framework serves as a practical and reliable evaluation tool for diagnosing content consistency and benchmarking model performance in real-world I2I systems.
